[ASSISTANT_SAID] Chest auscultation has a long history, dating back to the time of Hippocrates.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Widespread use of chest auscultation began with the invention of the stethoscope by René Laënnec in 1816.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] During the second half of the 20th century, technological advances in imaging shifted interest away from auscultation.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Modern computer-assisted techniques have improved the precision of recording and analysis of lung sounds.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The correlation of acoustic indexes with measures of lung mechanics has increased the clinical usefulness of auscultation.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] This review provides an overview of lung auscultation in the light of modern concepts of lung acoustics.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The traditional nomenclature for lung sounds is imprecise.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The International Lung Sounds Association proposed a new terminology.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The term "rale" was replaced with "crackle" in the new terminology.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] "Crackle" can be defined acoustically and does not suggest any means or site of generation.
